Esa proporción, que depende <em>solo del: That proportion, which depends only on the angle and not on the size, is what we call a trigonometric ratio. There are three main ones:
Ese es el seno: el cateto <em>opuesto</e: That is the sine: the opposite leg over the hypotenuse. The cosine uses the adjacent one.
Eso es la tangente. Seno y coseno llevan: That is the tangent. Sine and cosine have the hypotenuse in the denominator, and that is why they never exceed 1.
Hay tres ángulos que salen una y otra ve: There are three angles that come up again and again, and it pays to have them in your head: 30°, 45° and 60°. There is no need to memorise six loose numbers, because all six come out of two very simple drawings. The 45° one comes from cutting a square along the diagonal; the 30° and 60° ones, from cutting an equilateral triangle in half. With Pythagoras in those two figures every value in the table appears, and that is why they always carry roots of 2 or of 3.
La trigonometría nace de una observación: Trigonometry is born of one observation: if two right-angled triangles have the same acute angle, they are similar, and then the proportions between their sides are identical even though the triangles are of different sizes.
La trigonometría se inventó mirando al c: Trigonometry was invented looking at the sky. Hipparchus of Nicaea (second century BC) built the first table of chords to work out the positions of the stars, and Ptolemy perfected it in the Almagest. The word sine is an accident of translation: the Indians called it jya-ardha (half-chord), the Arabs transcribed it as jiba, and on passing into Latin it was confused with jaib, meaning “bay” or “bosom”. So we say “sine” because of a twelfth-century slip.

Que $\\operatorname{sen}^2\\alpha+\\cos^: That $\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=1$ is no more than Pythagoras' theorem on a circle of radius 1, and that is why it appears the moment something is conserved. In a pendulum, the energy is shared between kinetic and potential, changing at every instant, but the sum stays put: the same structure. When you see that identity, think “this is Pythagoras in disguise”.
Resolver triángulos es cómo se mide lo q: Solving triangles is how you measure what cannot be reached. A surveyor works out the height of a mountain by measuring an angle from two known points; that is how every map was made before satellites, chaining triangles across a whole country, and that is how Everest was first measured in 1852, to within a few metres and without setting foot on it. A carpenter cutting a staircase, a fitter deciding the tilt of some solar panels and a crane working out its reach all make the same calculation.
